params.name: target_file
params.description: Project-relative location of the document to inspect. Choose a single document, including its extension, rather than a folder or a wildcard. The reply repeats the resolved location so similarly named documents can be distinguished before their contents are used. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: starting_row
params.description: First numbered row to include, counting from one. Omit this value to begin at the top of the document. A starting row beyond the end yields an empty slice with the actual row count, allowing the caller to distinguish an exhausted document from a missing one. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

params.name: row_budget
params.description: Largest number of rows to return in this slice. Long documents can be explored with several adjacent slices instead of crowding unrelated context out of the conversation. The reply says whether additional rows remain and gives the next starting row. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

params.name: include_revision
params.description: Attach the document revision marker to the reply when true. This marker is an opaque comparison value rather than a timestamp, and should be carried forward unchanged when preparing an edit based on the returned text. It does not reveal any other document. Supply a JSON true or false value rather than a word such as yes or a number such as one. The tool reports the setting it applied so the caller can distinguish an explicit choice from any behavior used when an optional setting is absent.

sample:1.label: write_file
sample:1.note: Invented example text for the fictional Lantern demonstration.

params.name: destination_file
params.description: Project-relative location that will receive the complete document. Parent folders must already exist so a spelling mistake does not silently create a second directory tree. The returned location can be compared with the requested one before reporting success. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: document_text
params.description: Complete replacement text, with line endings included as they should appear on disk. An empty string deliberately creates an empty document. This input represents the whole document rather than a patch, and the reply reports its saved row count and revision. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: expected_revision
params.description: Revision from the most recent read of an existing document. A mismatch stops the save and describes the conflict without merging unrelated changes. Omit this only when creating a document that does not already exist under the create-only setting. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: create_only
params.description: Whether this operation must create a previously absent document. Set true for a new file and false for an intentional replacement with an expected revision. The distinction makes accidental replacement visible in the request itself, before any document is changed. Supply a JSON true or false value rather than a word such as yes or a number such as one. The tool reports the setting it applied so the caller can distinguish an explicit choice from any behavior used when an optional setting is absent.

sample:2.label: edit_file
sample:2.note: Invented example text for the fictional Lantern demonstration.

params.name: document_file
params.description: Project-relative document to change after inspecting its current contents. This operation edits one document at a time so the result can name the exact document and revision affected. Directory locations and wildcard expressions are rejected rather than expanded. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: matching_passage
params.description: Nonempty literal passage that identifies the intended change. Include enough surrounding words or punctuation to distinguish similar passages. Matching is case-sensitive and does not interpret regular expressions, escape sequences, or approximate spelling as instructions. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: replacement_passage
params.description: Text that takes the place of the matched passage. Use an empty string to remove that passage, and include any desired whitespace explicitly. Surrounding text is preserved, making the resulting excerpt useful for checking that the intended boundary was chosen. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: occurrence_number
params.description: One-based occurrence to replace when the same passage appears several times. Without this input, exactly one match is required. The result reports the number of matches found and the occurrence changed so repeated sections can be handled deliberately. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

sample:3.label: run_command
sample:3.note: Invented example text for the fictional Lantern demonstration.

params.name: shell_line
params.description: Command line to execute for a specific development check or local transformation. Quote document names containing spaces according to the selected shell. The command is recorded with its result so a later explanation can connect an observed exit value to the exact operation. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: working_folder
params.description: Project-relative folder in which the command begins. Choose the folder containing the relevant package or configuration instead of relying on a remembered shell location. A missing folder prevents execution and returns a startup error with no process output. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: duration_seconds
params.description: Maximum elapsed duration before the running process is stopped. Use a positive whole number suited to the check being run. A duration limit is reported separately from a normal nonzero exit, because partial output alone cannot establish that the check completed. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

params.name: output_budget
params.description: Maximum number of output characters retained in the reply. When output is larger, the reply keeps its beginning and end and marks the omitted middle. The process exit value remains available even when most of the output is omitted from the conversation. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

sample:4.note: Invented example text for the fictional Lantern demonstration.

params.name: needle_text
params.description: Literal text to locate, including spaces when a complete phrase is useful. The search treats punctuation as ordinary characters and does not expand regular expressions. An empty needle is rejected because it would match every position without helping locate a particular fact. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: search_folder
params.description: Project-relative folder whose documents should be searched. Nested folders are included unless excluded by the filename ending. Choose the smallest useful area so a result budget is spent on relevant code rather than generated output or unrelated examples. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: filename_ending
params.description: Optional filename suffix such as .js or .md that limits eligible documents. This is a literal ending rather than a wildcard language. Omit it to consider all readable text documents in the chosen area, with binary documents skipped and counted in the reply. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: match_budget
params.description: Maximum number of matching excerpts returned across all documents. Reaching this budget adds a partial-results marker instead of claiming no further matches exist. Each excerpt includes its document and row number, allowing subsequent reads to inspect the surrounding context. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

sample:5.label: list_directory
sample:5.note: Invented example text for the fictional Lantern demonstration.

params.name: directory_target
params.description: Project-relative folder to inspect, using a dot for the project root. This location is resolved before entries are listed, and the resolved folder is returned in the reply. A document location produces a type error rather than a misleading one-entry folder listing. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: nesting_depth
params.description: Number of folder levels to include, starting at one for immediate entries only. A positive ceiling keeps a large tree from consuming the entire reply. Each nested entry includes its relative location so identical names in different folders remain distinguishable. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

params.name: entry_budget
params.description: Maximum number of entries to include in the complete reply. The result states whether more entries were available after this budget was reached. Counts describe entries actually visited and do not pretend to measure the full size of an unfinished directory traversal. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

sample:6.note: Invented example text for the fictional Lantern demonstration.

params.name: reference_address
params.description: Complete public HTTP or HTTPS address to retrieve for a specific reference. Include the document location rather than a search phrase. The reply lists the final address after redirects so a caller can verify that the returned body belongs to the intended reference. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: body_budget
params.description: Maximum number of body characters retained after decoding the response as text. Truncated responses include a visible omission marker and the retained character count. A small budget is useful for checking a status or heading before requesting a longer reference excerpt. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

params.name: redirect_ceiling
params.description: Largest number of redirects allowed before retrieval stops. Zero requires the original address to answer directly. If the ceiling is exceeded, the reply reports the redirect chain observed so far and does not present an intermediate response as the requested document. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

params.name: decision_question
params.description: Question in ordinary language that explains the decision the user needs to make. Include enough project context to distinguish it from earlier questions. Avoid packing unrelated decisions into one prompt, since the resulting answer should be usable as one clear project preference. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: suggested_choices
params.description: Short text choices that describe meaningfully different outcomes for the project. Each entry should make sense without reading an internal identifier. The written-answer option remains available, so a suggested choice is never treated as the only possible response. Supply a JSON list, keeping each entry separate instead of joining entries into a comma-separated string. Order is retained where it carries meaning; an empty list is explicit and is different from leaving the optional field out of the request.

params.name: decision_context
params.description: Brief explanation of what changes depending on the answer. Describe the visible consequence or implementation constraint rather than internal tool mechanics. This context accompanies the question and helps the user respond without needing to reconstruct the preceding conversation. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: checklist_items
params.description: Ordered entries with a short task sentence and a state of waiting, active, or done. Each entry should describe an observable piece of work rather than an aspiration. Keep completed work in the list when it helps explain what remains, and remove it deliberately when it no longer helps. params.name: checklist_revision
params.description: Revision marker from the previous checklist reply, carried forward unchanged. A stale marker prevents replacement so an older update cannot erase newer progress. Omit it for the first checklist in a new task, which starts with no previously stored entries. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: progress_note
params.description: One short explanation of why the checklist changed. Mention a finished check, a discovered dependency, or a concrete scope adjustment when relevant. The note accompanies the list for readers and is not interpreted as another task or as evidence that a command succeeded. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: board_key
params.description: Identifier of the fictional project board to inspect. A board groups work items for one exercise and is named explicitly in every request. The reply repeats this key so entries from a different board cannot be casually combined with the current project checklist. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: state_filter
params.description: State to include: waiting, active, or done. Omit the filter to include all states on the selected board. An unsupported value returns a filter error instead of an empty list, keeping a spelling mistake distinguishable from a board with no matching work. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: page_size
params.description: Maximum number of work items on this page of the listing. The reply includes a continuation marker when another page is available. A page may contain fewer entries than requested without proving the board is empty, so use the marker to decide whether to continue. Supply a whole JSON number in the unit named here, without a quoted number or a unit suffix. Fractions and negative values are rejected instead of rounded or converted silently, so the accepted value can be compared directly with the request.

params.name: continuation_key
params.description: Opaque marker returned by an earlier listing with the same board and filters. Pass it unchanged to request the next page. Changing the board or filters starts a new listing and requires omitting this marker so unrelated page positions are not combined. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: comment_text

This operation stores the supplied text without changing item state, interpreting checklist marks, or notifying any real project service. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.

params.name: client_marker
params.description: Caller-chosen value identifying this particular comment submission. Reuse the same marker when retrying an uncertain result so the server can return the earlier comment instead of creating a duplicate. Use a fresh marker for a different comment, even on the same item. Supply this value as ordinary text in a JSON string, preserving meaningful spaces and punctuation. A document excerpt containing quotation marks or line breaks still belongs in one string; those characters are data rather than extra fields in the request.
